raw_text:
Great—here’s a practical 12-week couch-to-5K plan tailored for a 24-year-old male with exercise-induced asthma, aiming to complete a 5K in 12 weeks. It emphasizes gradual progression, proper warm-ups, warm-downs, and asthma considerations (including SABA use, airway-warming strategies, and intensity monitoring). The plan includes run/walk intervals, strength sessions, and key weekly progressions. You can adjust based on how the client feels and any medical guidance.

Assumptions and safety notes
- Medical clearance: already cleared; ensure clearance before starting or if symptoms worsen.
- Inhaler use: client should have access to their SABA and use it per physician guidance before or during workouts if needed.
- Warm-up priority: each session starts with a 5–10 minute dynamic warm-up and ends with a 5–10 minute cool-down and light mobility.
- Asthma management: avoid prolonged high-intensity bursts in cold air; if temperatures are cold, consider indoor or well-warmed outdoor sessions. If symptoms arise (cough, chest tightness, wheeze, shortness of breath not relieved by SABA within a few minutes), pause and use inhaler, then reassess.
- Training load: if any fever, infection, or significant fatigue, scale back.
- Injury prevention: include mobility and core work 2x/week to support running mechanics.

Program structure
- 12 weeks, 3 main running days per week (with optional cross-training and 2 light strength days).
- Week 1 is foundation; Week 2–4 gradually increase running volume; Week 5 introduce longer continuous segments; Week 6 cutback week; Weeks 7–12 build to race-pace readiness with a tolerance for mild progression and one longer run each week.
- Run/Walk approach: run intervals interspersed with walking to stay within comfortable intensity zones and reduce asthma risk during high-impact bouts.

Phase 1: Foundation and technique (Weeks 1–3)
Goals: establish consistency, proper warm-up, aerobic base, and running form; reduce asthma-trigger risk with run/walk.

Weekly layout (example): 3 running days (R), 2 cross-training/active recovery days (XT), 2 rest or mobility days.

Week 1
- Session A: Run/Walk 20 minutes
  - 5-minute dynamic warm-up (leg swings, hip circles, ankle mobility), 5–10 minutes easy jog
  - Run 1 min, walk 1.5 min x 6 cycles = 18 minutes total run time
  - 5-minute cool-down walk, 5 minutes gentle mobility
- Session B: Run/Walk 18–22 minutes with more walking
  - Warm-up; Run 1 min 15 sec, Walk 2 min x 7 cycles
  - Cool-down
- Session C: Optional cross-training 20–30 minutes (cycling, rowing, or brisk walking) at easy intensity; core work 10 minutes (planks, dead bugs, birddogs)

Strength (2x/Week, non-consecutive)
- 2 sets of 10–12 reps: bodyweight squats, glute bridges, lunges (alternate legs), push-ups (modify on knees if needed)
- 2–3 core moves: dead bug, side planks 20–30 seconds, bird-dogs

Week 2
- Session A: Run/Walk 22–25 minutes
  - Run 1 min 30 sec, Walk 1 min 30 sec x 9 cycles
- Session B: Run/Walk 20–25 minutes
  - Run 1 min 45 sec, Walk 1 min 15 sec x 8 cycles
- Session C: Cross-train 25–30 minutes, plus mobility

Strength: same pattern; add light resistance if available (dumbbell goblet squats 2x10, rows 2x10)

Week 3
- Session A: Run/Walk 26–28 minutes
  - Run 2 minutes, Walk 1 minute x 8 cycles
- Session B: Run/Walk 22–28 minutes
  - Run 2 minutes, Walk 1 minute 30 sec x 9 cycles
- Session C: Cross-train 25–35 minutes (include hills if comfortable) or sport-like activity (swimming) at easy pace
Strength: 2 sets of 12 reps; include step-ups, farmer’s carries (short), greater plank holds 30–40 seconds

Phase 2: Build endurance and tolerance (Weeks 4–6)
Goals: increase continuous running duration, improve efficiency, maintain asthma control, introduce longer intervals.

Week 4
- Session A: Run 28–30 minutes with intervals
  - Warm-up; Run 3 minutes, Walk 1 minute x 6 cycles
- Session B: Run continuous 20–25 minutes easy
- Session C: Cross-train 30–40 minutes or fartlek style (short bursts of faster effort every 4 minutes, easy between)

Strength: add tempo emphasis on single-leg work; split squats, hip hinges, 2–3 sets

Week 5
- Session A: Run/Walk 30–32 minutes
  - Run 4 minutes, Walk 1 minute x 6 cycles
- Session B: Run continuous 24–28 minutes
- Session C: Cross-train 30–40 minutes; mobility and scapular stability

Strength: 2–3 sets, include plates or dumbbells if available (deadlift, Romanian deadlift 8–10 reps; overhead press 8–10; core)

Week 6 (Recovery/Deload Week)
- Session A: Run/Walk 24–28 minutes easy
  - Run 2–3 minutes, Walk 1–2 minutes x 6 cycles
- Session B: Run 20–25 minutes easy
- Session C: Cross-train 20–30 minutes easy; mobility and yoga flows
Strength: reduce volume to 1–2 sets; focus on form

Phase 3: Specific endurance and race preparation (Weeks 7–12)
Goals: solid continuous running endurance, longer single runs, practice race-pace, manage asthma with warm-ups.

Week 7
- Session A (Tempo-ish): Run 25–30 minutes with pick-ups
  - Warm-up; Run 5 minutes easy, then 3 x 2-minute moderate efforts with 2 minutes easy between, finish easy 5 minutes
- Session B: Longish run/walk 26–32 minutes continuous if comfortable; otherwise extend walk intervals gradually
- Session C: Cross-train or easy run 20–30 minutes

Week 8
- Session A: Run 30–34 minutes continuous if able; otherwise 3–4x5 minutes with 2-minute easy between
- Session B: Long run 26–34 minutes, try to hold a comfortable pace
- Session C: Mobility, core, 20 minutes

Week 9
- Session A: Run 34–38 minutes continuous (aim for at least 25–30 minutes nonstop if tolerance allows)
- Session B: Intervals: 4 x 4 minutes at a steady, moderately hard pace with 2–3 minutes easy
- Session C: Cross-train 30–40 minutes or easy run 20–25 minutes

Week 10
- Session A: Run 38–42 minutes continuous if comfortable; otherwise 3–4 x 8 minutes with 2–3 minutes easy
- Session B: Long run 28–40 minutes at easy pace
- Session C: Mobility and core 20 minutes

Week 11
- Session A: Race-pace readiness: 2 x 10 minutes at a pace close to goal 5K pace, with 3 minutes easy between; warm-up and cool-down
- Session B: Long run 30–45 minutes easy
- Session C: Easy cross-training or easy run 20–25 minutes

Week 12 (Taper and race week)
- Session A: Short, sharp run: 20–25 minutes total with 2 x 3 minutes at goal pace, 3 minutes easy between
- Session B: Easy 15–20 minutes, plus strides (6 x 15–20 seconds at faster pace with full recovery)
- Session C: Rest or very light mobility; mental rehearsal and race strategy

Final race week considerations
- Easy, well-warmed pre-race: light jog 5–10 minutes, dynamic warm-up, and dynamic strides
- Inhale/exhale technique: nasal breathing optional but focus on relaxed shoulders and diaphragmatic breathing; use inhaler as prescribed before start if recommended
- Pacing: start conservatively, aim to settle into goal pace by halfway; finish strong if possible
- Post-race recovery: cool-down walk, gentle stretching, hydration, and if sore, light mobility and rest

Weekly structure (example for a typical week)
- Monday: Run Day 1 (as per weeks 1–12 plan) + 10–15 minutes mobility
- Tuesday: Strength/Core (20–35 minutes) or cross-training
- Wednesday: Run Day 2 (as per weeks 1–12 plan)
- Thursday: Rest or light mobility
- Friday: Run Day 3 or Cross-training (as per plan) or rest
- Saturday: Cross-training or optional easy run (20–30 minutes)
- Sunday: Rest or light mobility

Nutrition and recovery tips
- Hydration: aim for consistent hydration; carry water on longer sessions if needed
- Pre-run fueling: light snack 60–90 minutes before running (banana, yogurt, small toast with peanut butter)
- Post-run: protein-rich snack within 60 minutes (30–40 g protein if possible) and carb for glycogen replenishment
- Asthma considerations: if exercise-induced symptoms are triggered by cold air, consider a lightweight scarf/buffer or warm-up indoors for 5–10 minutes before heading out; humidify indoor air if possible
- Sleep and stress: target 7–9 hours of sleep; manage stress to aid recovery

Monitoring and progression
- Use RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion) or talk test to gauge intensity: you should be able to speak in short phrases during easy runs; if you’re gasping, ease off
- Track symptoms: record asthma symptoms before, during, and after sessions; scale intensity and note any SABA use
- Adjust progression: if fatigue or asthma symptoms increase, reduce volume by 10–20% and maintain intensity at easy levels until recovered

Optional: beginner-friendly 5K race plan structure
- Weeks 9–12 emphasize longer continuous running and one tempo/race-pace session per week
- The final week eases down to allow full recovery and taper for race day
